finding.claim: collect uses forEach with an async callback and returns immediately, so results is always empty and async errors are never caught.
finding.title: async forEach never awaited returns empty results

verifier.reason: The code at src/analytics.ts:6 uses tasks.forEach with an async callback whose awaited pushes at src/analytics.ts:7 are not awaited by collect, which returns the still-unpopulated results array at src/analytics.ts:12, and the surrounding try/catch at src/analytics.ts:5 cannot catch the callbacks' later async rejections.

finding.claim: validate uses || instead of && so each condition is always true and every payload reports missing id and value.
finding.title: validation condition always true

verifier.reason: The conditions at src/validation.ts:8 and src/validation.ts:11 use !== undefined || !== null, which is tautologically true for any value, so both errors are always pushed for every payload.

finding.claim: buildSummary appends to module-level totals on every call then summarizes totals, so a second call double-counts prior entries.
finding.title: module accumulator makes repeated summary double-count

verifier.reason: buildSummary at src/ledger.ts:12-15 calls post(entries), which pushes onto the module-level totals declared at src/ledger.ts:6-9, and then iterates totals rather than only its argument with no reset inside buildSummary, so a second call re-includes prior entries.

finding.claim: rotateToken does not await store.save before store.get, so the read can race the write and return a stale token.
finding.title: missing await on async save before read

verifier.reason: Confirmed: store.save returns Promise<void> at src/session.ts:2 but is called without await at src/session.ts:11 before store.get is returned at src/session.ts:12, so the read can race the pending write.

finding.claim: start replaces this.timer with a new setInterval without clearing any existing interval, leaking the prior timer.
finding.title: interval handle replaced without clearing

verifier.reason: The code at src/scheduler.ts:7-11 assigns this.timer = setInterval(...) with no preceding clearInterval or guard, so a second start() call orphans the prior interval handle.

finding.claim: sort without a comparator sorts numbers lexicographically, so sortScores and topScore return wrong order.
finding.title: numeric sort without comparator

verifier.reason: The code at src/scores.ts:2 calls scores.slice().sort() with no comparator, so JavaScript sorts numbers lexicographically, and topScore at src/scores.ts:7 returns the last element of that incorrectly ordered array.

finding.claim: pageSlice slices to end+1 instead of end, returning size+1 elements per page.
finding.title: page slice off-by-one returns extra item

verifier.reason: At src/paging.ts:9 end is start+size and at src/paging.ts:10 slice(start, end+1) is returned, so the exclusive slice bound yields size+1 elements when available.

finding.claim: normalizeSettings uses || fallback so legitimate 0 values are replaced by defaults, contradicting the stated 0-is-legitimate rule.
finding.title: falsy fallback discards legitimate zero

verifier.reason: normalizeSettings at src/settings.ts:13-14 uses `raw.pageSize || 20` and `raw.budgetCents || 1000`, so an input of 0 is replaced by the default, while src/settings.ts:18 states 0 is a legitimate value and src/settings.ts:20-21 shows the correct null-only fallback pattern.
